title: Minimal Leakage Class Relating IND–CPLA and IND–aCPLA
summary: A general reduction is unavailable with decryption-enabled nonce reuse, and nonce-independent leakage supports only restrictive cases; characterizing a minimal sufficient leakage class remains open.

formal_statement.body: For pairs of leakage classes $L_E$ and $L_D$ drawn from general function classes, characterize a corresponding class $L_{ED}$ and formalize a sense in which it is minimal while still containing the leakage needed to relate $\mathrm{IND\!-\!CPLA}$ and $\mathrm{IND\!-\!aCPLA}$ security. A general reduction between these notions is unavailable when a decryption oracle permits an adversary to reuse a nonce, while reductions for nonce-independent leakage require more restrictive settings.

scope.domain: Leakage-resilient authenticated encryption and security relations between IND–CPLA and IND–aCPLA.
assumptions: The leakage classes L_E and L_D are drawn from general function classes.
parameters: L_E and L_D: input leakage classes whose pair determines the target class
L_ED: the corresponding leakage class intended to contain the leakage needed for the security relation
scope.unresolved_remainder: Characterize L_ED for general pairs of leakage classes and formalize a suitable minimality notion while retaining the leakage needed to relate the two security notions.

progress.summary: The source explicitly calls characterizing a suitably minimal L_ED for general pairs of leakage classes an open problem. It identifies decryption-enabled nonce reuse as blocking a general reduction and nonce-independent leakage as yielding only restrictive cases.
